hero.alt: Satya Nadella on the Ignite stage under three panels reading 'Where you build', 'Where your data lives' and 'Where your agents go to work'
hero.caption: Satya Nadella frames Microsoft's AI platform: where you build, where your data lives, and where your agents go to work

items.alt: Copilot app demo with Work IQ, Salesforce, Outlook and Teams plugins, drafting and sending a Teams message about a stalled deal
items.title: Copilot becomes the place work starts
items.what: The demo ran entirely inside the Copilot app. It used Work IQ to find the biggest stalled deal, pulled context from Salesforce and Outlook, then drafted and sent a Teams message, all from one conversation.
items.means: The app you open first in the morning changes. Instead of switching between CRM, email and chat, you describe the outcome and Copilot works across the tools. Microsoft now calls this the new operating system for work.

items.alt: Autopilot demo: a user asks Copilot to track client outreach and draft follow-ups for approval, with a timeline of completed tasks
items.title: Autopilot: an agent that keeps working
items.what: A user asks Copilot to track three clients, draft follow-ups when someone goes quiet for a week, and send a weekly performance update. The timeline shows Autopilot preparing meeting briefs and logging client conversations in Dynamics 365, each one reviewed by the user.
items.means: This is delegation rather than assistance: you set a standing instruction and approve the results. Expect job descriptions to start including how well you brief and supervise agents.

items.alt: On-stage Copilot demo in which Copilot reasons for over a minute and saves a keynote outline as a Word document to OneDrive
items.title: Office documents become an output of a conversation
items.what: On stage, Copilot reasoned for over a minute, mapped a set of topics to a keynote structure, and saved the result as a Word document in OneDrive. That is Office in Copilot, now generally available.
items.means: First drafts take minutes, not hours. The value moves to the brief you give and the judgement you apply to the draft, which is where professionals can still stand out.

items.alt: Chart comparing decision models on score versus speed, showing Microsoft Decision 1.1 six points higher and 2.2 times faster than version 1
items.title: Microsoft's own models go head to head
items.what: Microsoft-Decision-1.1 was shown scoring six points higher and running 2.2 times faster than its predecessor on the Artificial Analysis decision index. It's one of a new family of in-house MAI models for code, security, images and decisions.
items.means: Microsoft is reducing its reliance on any single AI lab. More competition between models generally means lower prices and faster responses for the AI built into the tools you use.

items.alt: Satya Nadella on stage in front of a slide introducing the AI Transparency Initiative
items.title: Trust gets its own slide
items.what: Nadella introduced the AI Transparency Initiative, an industry effort towards a common approach to AI transparency, security and governance. Copilot, IQ, Perception, Azure and Microsoft's MAI models are named as part of Microsoft's commitment.
items.means: As agents take on real work, companies will only scale them if they can audit what the agents did. Governance is becoming a selling point, and a career path.

items.alt: Slide titled 'Our community-first AI infrastructure plan' with five commitments on electricity prices, water, jobs, tax base and local AI training
items.title: AI's physical footprint is now a keynote topic
items.what: Microsoft set out a community-first data centre plan: pay its way so data centres don't raise local electricity prices, use less water and replenish more than it uses, create local jobs, add to the tax base, and invest in local AI training.
items.means: Building data centres for AI now depends on public approval as much as technology. Energy, sustainability and local-policy expertise are becoming part of the AI story, which opens doors well beyond tech roles.
